result.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
result.summary: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. First, we introduce SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER-based papers together with the data and resources required to reproduce their findings. Second, we create an AI agent that successfully reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, while providing executable baselines for further analysis. Third, we develop an agentic analysis pipeline to test the robustness of the medical findings by identifying analytical choices underlying each finding, proposing defensible alternatives, and rerunning the analysis to determine whether those choices affect the conclusion. Across published papers in SEER-Repro, our pipeline identifies potentially consequential analytical choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings and flags them for expert review. These results show how LLM agents can support scientific review by reproducing findings, systematically testing their robustness, and directing expert attention toward potentially consequential analytical choices.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以 SEER 癌症登记数据库为基础构建 SEER-Repro 基准（20 篇已发表论文及复现所需数据资源），并开发 LLM agent 流水线自动复现 2,190 条原子论断（成功率 77.4%），进而识别各结论背后的分析选择、提出可辩护的替代方案并重跑分析，判断这些选择是否改变结论。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「定位隐含分析选择—生成替代方案—重跑以检验结论是否改变」的稳健性流程，可能与 LVR 中判断 latent 推理步骤或视觉证据筛选是否对答案有因果贡献的反事实/消融式评价存在概念联系，可供核查；但领域与视觉多模态推理距离较远，联系属推测。
